# Three kinases, one question

*Generated by `scripts/build_pipelines_md.py` on 2026-10-30 18:11 UTC. Every number is read from `data/derived/`; do not edit by hand.*

## The question, asked three times

A preclinical resistance screen produces a hit list. That list is the product
of two things: which variants the mutagen can **supply**, and which of those
the drug **selects**. Write it as

> P(v) ∝ S_mutagen(v) · exp(βσ(v))

`S` comes from the genetic code plus the mutagen's six-class pyrimidine
spectrum. `σ` comes from a **chemistry-free** atlas, one built without a
mutagen, so it reports selection uncontaminated by supply. Comparing the two
tells us which variants a given chemistry cannot reach, and whether the
weighting it applies to the rest changes their order.

The same comparison is run on three kinases. Each contributes something the
others cannot.

| | KRAS G12C | ALK | MET |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What it adds** | a panel with two-step variants in it | three drugs, three mutagens, a dose series | nucleotide-level hits and two screens sharing one mutagen |
| **Chemistry-free side** | Feng 2022 Twist synthetic library | Oh 2026 prime-editing atlas | Estevam 2024 saturation DMS |
| **Chemistry-biased side** | Awad 2021 clinical cohort + accompanying *in vitro* scan; Tang 2022 ENU; Diaz 2025 CBE+ABE | Doi 2022 Mutazyme II; Tangpeerachaikul 2025 ENU; Takei 2025 ePCR | Tiedt 2011 ENU, two arms |
| **TKIs** | sotorasib, adagrasib | alectinib, lorlatinib, zotizalkib (neladalkib by proxy) | NVP-BVU972 (type I), AMG 458 (type II) |
| **σ definition** | normalized Z-score | Oh Resistance score (Fitness is orthogonal, not subtracted) | ROSACE effect **minus the DMSO arm** |
| **Universe used for ranking** | 1,205 class-forced | 1,427 class-forced | 5,458 missense, not restricted to class-forced |
| **Why the universes differ** | the ALK and KRAS benchmarks rank within a class-forced set so that every variant carries one supply weight | | the MET audit ranks over the whole atlas and classifies reachability per variant, because its library contains two-step variants worth counting |
| **Library reach** | includes multi-nucleotide variants | one-step variants only, by prime-edit design | includes multi-nucleotide variants |

The σ row is the one most easily got wrong. Oh's Resistance score is already
log(drug / untreated), so growth is divided out before we see it and its
Fitness axis is orthogonal; subtracting it again would be double-counting.
Estevam's score is computed per arm against that arm's own starting pool, so
the drug arms still carry growth and the DMSO arm correlates with them at
r ≈ 0.8. Subtracting DMSO there reproduces Oh's quantity. Same principle,
opposite arithmetic.

## Codon tables: how each was derived and checked

Reachability is a codon computation, so every claim rests on these.

| | source | span | verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| **KRAS-4A** | RefSeq NM_033360.4, CDS 191..760 | 189 codons | ClinVar-anchored at panel residues; checked against the Feng atlas wild-type residues |
| **ALK** | Oh 2026 Table S11, EML4-ALK variant-1 WT construct | 331 codons, 1058–1388 | read in-frame off the construct the atlas was built in; every position checked against the atlas's own wild-type residue |
| **MET** | RefSeq NM_000245.2, CDS 188..4360 | 287 codons, 1059–1345 | the record Tiedt's tables are numbered against; three independent checks |

Two notes that matter for reproduction:

- **KRAS codon 12** is GGT (Gly) in the reference table but the Feng library
  carries G12C, so the pipeline overrides it to TGT (Cys). Without that
  override the reachability of C12F is wrong.
- **ALK numbering** is local in the published tables. The offset to canonical
  numbering is re-derived from the data rather than assumed.

### The decisive comparisons, with their statistics

| finding | pipeline | statistic |
|---|---|---|
| C>G hits exceed what germline-ENU supply predicts | ALK | P = 4.7e-05 against the model-implied null (β = 1) |
| …but are unremarkable once supply is removed | ALK | P = 0.64 against a selection-only null |
| …and C>G is supplied anyway at practical depth | ALK | P(detect) = 0.86 at the germline rate |
| One mutagen, two drugs, different class compositions | MET | χ² = 12.4, df = 5, P = 0.029 |
| Every reachable route at one codon was recovered | MET | 5 of 6 routes, across classes spanning 7.3-fold in supply |
| σ transports unevenly to a Ba/F3 screen | ALK | Spearman 0.82 / 0.51 / 0.17 (zot / alec / lor) |
| σ moves across the atlas's own dose range | ALK | median Spearman 0.39 low-vs-high dose |

## Reading the results through the framework

The three pipelines agree on a single mechanism: **chemistry sets what can
appear, selection sets the order of what does.**

**Why hits are recovered well.** Wherever a variant's route is supplied at
all, the chemistry-free ranking predicts it. Doi's five class-forced hits all
land in the Mutazyme-simulated top-120; every Tiedt hit is in the MET atlas
at a median rank inside the top 5%. Supply does not need to be large, only
non-zero: at N = 10⁷ and μ = 10⁻⁴ even ENU's rarest class clears the
detection bound, which is why rare-class variants still turn up.

**Why the weighting adds nothing.** Once every class clears that bound, the
magnitude of the class rate stops gating the output. The benchmark shows no
gain from log S + σ over σ alone on any anchor, and the MET two-screen
control shows the composition of a hit list tracking the drug rather than the
mutagen. These are the same fact seen twice.

**Why some variants are never recovered.** Two reasons, and they differ in
kind. A base-editor pair has an exactly zero rate for four of six classes, so
no depth recovers those variants. A two-step variant has a non-zero but
heavily suppressed rate, so depth and rounds matter: a single-round protocol
will usually miss it, a multi-round one may not, which is why error-prone PCR
compound screens recover multi-nucleotide events at all.

**What the framework does not settle.** σ itself is measured with limited
resolution, unevenly across drugs and across concentration, so the ranking
half of the decomposition inherits that. The reachability half does not: it
depends on codon tables and a published spectrum, both of which are exact.

  and DOI, but no full author list or page range; Crossref and PubMed were
  unreachable from the analysis environment when they were added.
- Y1230F was not recovered by the MET screen and is not explained by supply,
  selection or fitness. Reported as an open discrepancy.
- The zotizalkib arm of the Oh atlas best-matches its middle concentration
  rather than its lowest, unlike the other two drugs. Reported without an
